name: Adam
summary: The first human, made in God's image and placed in the garden of Eden.
dateNote: Genesis 5:5 gives his age as 930; the start date is not fixed.

name: Noah
summary: A righteous man who built the ark and was saved through the Flood with his family.
dateNote: Genesis 9:29 gives his age as 950.

name: Terah
summary: Father of Abram, who led his family from Ur toward Canaan and died in Haran.
dateNote: Lived 205 years and died before Abram left Haran (Genesis 11:32; Acts 7:4).

name: Abraham
summary: Called by God to leave his homeland; God promised him land, descendants and blessing for all nations.
dateNote: Lived 175 years (Genesis 25:7).

name: Sarah
summary: Abraham's wife, who bore Isaac in her old age as God had promised.
dateNote: Ten years younger than Abraham; died at 127 (Genesis 17:17; 23:1).

name: Hagar
summary: Sarah's Egyptian servant and mother of Ishmael, whom God saw and cared for in the wilderness.

name: Ishmael
summary: Abraham's first son, through Hagar. God promised to make him a great nation.
dateNote: Born when Abram was 86; lived 137 years (Genesis 16:16; 25:17).

name: Lot
summary: Abraham's nephew, who settled near Sodom and was rescued before its destruction.

name: Isaac
summary: The son of promise, born to Abraham and Sarah; father of Jacob and Esau.
dateNote: Born when Abraham was 100; lived 180 years (Genesis 21:5; 35:28).

name: Rebekah
summary: Isaac's wife, from Abraham's family in Haran; mother of Jacob and Esau.

name: Esau
summary: Jacob's twin brother, who sold his birthright; ancestor of the Edomites.

name: Jacob
summary: Isaac's son, renamed Israel; his twelve sons became the tribes of Israel.
dateNote: Born when Isaac was 60; 130 when he went to Egypt; lived 147 years (Genesis 25:26; 47:9, 28).

name: Job
summary: Blameless and upright, he lost everything yet would not curse God, and was answered out of the whirlwind.

name: Leah
summary: Jacob's first wife, mother of six tribes including Levi and Judah.

name: Rachel
summary: Jacob's beloved wife, mother of Joseph and Benjamin.

name: Judah
summary: Fourth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the royal tribe of Judah.

name: Joseph
summary: Sold into slavery by his brothers, raised to rule Egypt, and used by God to save his family from famine.
dateNote: Aged 39 when Jacob arrived in Egypt; lived 110 years (Genesis 41:46, 53; 45:6; 50:26).

name: Moses
summary: Raised in Pharaoh's household, called by God at the burning bush to lead Israel out of Egypt and give them God's law.
dateNote: 80 at the Exodus; died at 120 (Exodus 7:7; Deuteronomy 34:7).

name: Aaron
summary: Moses' older brother and spokesman, and Israel's first high priest.
dateNote: 83 at the Exodus; died at 123 (Exodus 7:7; Numbers 33:39).

name: Miriam
summary: Sister of Moses and Aaron, who led Israel in song after the Red Sea crossing.
dateNote: Birth year estimated; she watched over the infant Moses (Exodus 2:4).

name: Joshua
summary: Moses' assistant, one of the two faithful spies, and his successor who led Israel into Canaan.
dateNote: Died at 110 (Joshua 24:29); birth year estimated.

name: Caleb
summary: One of the twelve spies, who trusted God's promise and urged Israel to take the land.

name: Jethro
summary: Moses' father-in-law, who sheltered him in Midian and later advised him in the wilderness.

name: Pharaoh of the Exodus
summary: The unnamed king who refused to let Israel go until the tenth plague.
dateNote: Not named in Scripture. The early date points to an 18th-dynasty king such as Amenhotep II; the late date points to Rameses II.

name: Rahab
summary: Hid Israel's spies in Jericho and was spared with her family when the city fell. Matthew names her among the ancestors of Jesus.

name: Deborah
summary: Prophetess who judged Israel under a palm tree and called Barak to fight Sisera.

name: Barak
summary: Led Israel's army from Mount Tabor against Sisera at Deborah's word.

name: Gideon
summary: A fearful farmer whom God called to free Israel from Midian with only three hundred men.

name: Samson
summary: Judge of great strength who fought the Philistines alone, was betrayed by Delilah, and died bringing down Dagon's temple.

name: Naomi
summary: Returned from Moab bereaved and bitter, and saw God's kindness through her daughter-in-law Ruth.

name: Boaz
summary: A worthy man of Bethlehem who redeemed Naomi's land and married Ruth; great-grandfather of David.

name: Ruth
summary: Left Moab to stay with Naomi and her God, married Boaz, and became great-grandmother of King David.

name: Eli
summary: Priest at Shiloh who raised the boy Samuel; he died when he heard the ark had been captured.
dateNote: Died at 98 (1 Samuel 4:15–18).

name: Hannah
summary: Prayed for a son at Shiloh, gave Samuel back to serve the Lord, and sang a song of praise.

name: Samuel
summary: The last judge, who led Israel back to God and anointed its first two kings, Saul and David.
dateNote: Birth estimated. He died before Saul did (1 Samuel 25:1).

name: Saul
summary: Israel's first king: chosen and anointed by Samuel, rejected for his disobedience, and killed in battle on Mount Gilboa.
dateNote: Birth estimated: his son Jonathan already led troops early in his reign (1 Samuel 13:2). Reigned about 1050–1010 BC; Acts 13:21 gives him forty years.

name: Jonathan
summary: Saul's son and David's loyal friend, who died with his father at Gilboa.

name: Jesse
summary: A man of Bethlehem, grandson of Ruth and Boaz, whose youngest son David became king.

name: Goliath
summary: Giant warrior from Gath who defied Israel's army until David killed him with a sling stone.

name: Bathsheba
summary: Wife of Uriah, taken by David; later his wife and the mother of Solomon.

name: David
summary: Shepherd, giant-slayer and Israel's greatest king, "a man after God's own heart," to whom God promised an everlasting kingdom.
dateNote: Thirty when he became king, and reigned forty years (2 Samuel 5:4).

name: Nathan
summary: Prophet who brought God's covenant promise to David and later confronted him over Bathsheba.

name: Solomon
summary: David's son, famed for his wisdom and wealth, who built the temple but turned to other gods in his old age.
dateNote: Birth estimated; he calls himself "a little child" when he becomes king (1 Kings 3:7).

name: Rehoboam
summary: Solomon's son, whose harsh answer split the kingdom; he kept only Judah and Benjamin.
dateNote: 41 when he became king; reigned 17 years (1 Kings 14:21), 931–913 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Jeroboam I
summary: First king of the northern kingdom, who set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.
dateNote: Reigned 22 years (1 Kings 14:20), 931–910 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Ahab
summary: King of Israel who, with Jezebel, promoted the worship of Baal and opposed Elijah.
dateNote: Reigned 22 years (1 Kings 16:29), 874–853 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Jezebel
summary: Phoenician princess and Ahab's queen, who persecuted the Lord's prophets.

name: Abijah
summary: Rehoboam's son, who fought Jeroboam and, as Chronicles tells it, cried to the Lord in battle and won.
dateNote: Reigned three years (1 Kings 15:2), 913–911 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Asa
summary: King of Judah who tore down idols and removed his grandmother from power for her Asherah pole, but in later years relied on Aram rather than the Lord.
dateNote: Reigned 41 years (1 Kings 15:10), 911–870 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Jehoshaphat
summary: Faithful king of Judah who sent teachers of the Law through the land, though he allied himself with Ahab.
dateNote: 35 when he became king; reigned 25 years (1 Kings 22:42), from 873 BC (at first alongside Asa) to 848 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Jehoram of Judah
summary: Jehoshaphat's son, who married Ahab's daughter Athaliah and followed the ways of Israel's kings.
dateNote: 32 when he became sole king in 848 BC; reigned eight years (2 Kings 8:17), after ruling alongside his father from 853 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Ahaziah of Judah
summary: Athaliah's son, killed by Jehu's men after a year as king while visiting Joram of Israel.
dateNote: 22 when he became king; reigned one year (2 Kings 8:26) and was killed in 841 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Athaliah
summary: Ahab's daughter, who seized Judah's throne and killed the royal family, all but the infant Joash.
dateNote: Ruled six years (2 Kings 11:3), 841–835 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are her reign.

name: Joash of Judah
summary: Hidden as a baby from Athaliah and crowned at seven, he repaired the temple, but after the priest Jehoiada died he turned away and was assassinated.
dateNote: Seven when he became king; reigned 40 years (2 Kings 11:21; 12:1), 835–796 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Amaziah
summary: Joash's son, who defeated Edom, then challenged Israel and was routed; he was later assassinated.
dateNote: 25 when he became king; reigned 29 years (2 Kings 14:2), 796–767 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Uzziah
summary: Long-reigning king of Judah whose strength turned to pride; he was struck with a skin disease for burning incense in the temple. Isaiah saw his vision of the Lord the year he died.
dateNote: 16 when he became king; reigned 52 years (2 Kings 15:2), from 792 BC (at first alongside Amaziah) to 740 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Jotham
summary: Uzziah's son, who ruled for his father during his illness and did right, though the people still worshipped at the high places.
dateNote: 25 when he became king, ruling for Uzziah from 750 BC; reigned 16 years (2 Kings 15:5, 33) and died about 732 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Ahaz
summary: Faithless king of Judah who, threatened by Aram and Israel, paid Assyria for help instead of trusting God; Isaiah gave him the sign of Immanuel.
dateNote: Reigned 16 years (2 Kings 16:2), 732–715 BC in Thiele's dating, after ruling alongside Jotham from 735 BC. Scripture gives his age, but it's hard to square with Hezekiah's, so these are his reign.

name: Manasseh
summary: Judah's longest-reigning king and its worst, who filled Jerusalem with idols and innocent blood; Chronicles tells of his repentance in captivity.
dateNote: 12 when he became king; reigned 55 years (2 Kings 21:1), from 697 BC (at first alongside Hezekiah) to 642 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Amon
summary: Manasseh's son, who followed his father's idols and was killed by his own servants.
dateNote: 22 when he became king; reigned two years (2 Kings 21:19), 642–640 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Jehoahaz of Judah
summary: Josiah's son, made king by the people after Megiddo and taken to Egypt by Pharaoh Neco three months later.
dateNote: 23 when he became king in 609 BC; reigned three months before Pharaoh Neco took him to Egypt, where he died (2 Kings 23:31–34). When he died isn't recorded, so this is his reign.

name: Jehoiakim
summary: Put on the throne by Pharaoh Neco, he burned Jeremiah's scroll and rebelled against Babylon.
dateNote: 25 when he became king; reigned 11 years (2 Kings 23:36), 609–598 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Jehoiachin
summary: Taken to Babylon after three months as king; in his old age Babylon's new king freed him and gave him a place at his table.
dateNote: 18 when he became king in 598 BC; reigned three months (2 Kings 24:8). Still alive in 561 BC, when Evil-merodach freed him (2 Kings 25:27–30); his death isn't recorded, so the bar ends there.

name: Nadab
summary: Jeroboam's son, killed by Baasha after two years, ending Jeroboam's line.
dateNote: Reigned two years (1 Kings 15:25), 910–909 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Baasha
summary: Took Israel's throne by killing Nadab and wiped out Jeroboam's house, but walked in Jeroboam's ways.
dateNote: Reigned 24 years (1 Kings 15:33), 909–886 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Elah
summary: Baasha's son, killed while drunk by his officer Zimri.
dateNote: Reigned two years (1 Kings 16:8), 886–885 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Zimri
summary: Chariot commander who killed Elah and reigned seven days, then burned the palace over himself as Omri's army closed in.
dateNote: Reigned seven days (1 Kings 16:15), in 885 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Omri
summary: Army commander who won the throne after a civil war, built Samaria as Israel's capital, and founded the dynasty of Ahab.
dateNote: Reigned 12 years (1 Kings 16:23), 885–874 BC in Thiele's dating, the first years against a rival, Tibni. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Ahaziah of Israel
summary: Ahab's son, who after a fall sent to ask Baal-zebub whether he would recover; Elijah said he would not.
dateNote: Reigned two years (1 Kings 22:51), 853–852 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Joram of Israel
summary: Ahab's son, who fought Moab alongside Jehoshaphat and was killed by Jehu at Jezreel.
dateNote: Reigned 12 years (2 Kings 3:1), 852–841 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Jehu
summary: Army commander anointed at Elisha's word, who wiped out Ahab's house and Baal's worshippers, but kept Jeroboam's golden calves.
dateNote: Reigned 28 years (2 Kings 10:36), 841–814 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Jehoahaz of Israel
summary: Jehu's son, under whom Aram ground Israel down until he sought the Lord's help.
dateNote: Reigned 17 years (2 Kings 13:1), 814–798 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Jehoash of Israel
summary: Wept at the dying Elisha's bedside, then beat Aram three times as the prophet foretold, and defeated Amaziah of Judah.
dateNote: Reigned 16 years (2 Kings 13:10), 798–782 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Jeroboam II
summary: Restored Israel's borders as Jonah had foretold; the wealth and injustice of his reign are the setting of Amos and Hosea.
dateNote: Reigned 41 years (2 Kings 14:23), counted from 793 BC, when he began alongside his father; sole king 782–753 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Zechariah of Israel
summary: Jeroboam II's son and the last of Jehu's line, killed by Shallum after six months, as God had told Jehu.
dateNote: Reigned six months (2 Kings 15:8), in 753 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Shallum
summary: Killed Zechariah and reigned a month before Menahem killed him.
dateNote: Reigned one month (2 Kings 15:13), in 752 BC in Thiele's dating.

name: Menahem
summary: Seized the throne in Samaria and paid the Assyrian king Pul a thousand talents of silver to keep it.
dateNote: Reigned ten years (2 Kings 15:17), 752–742 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Pekahiah
summary: Menahem's son, killed by his officer Pekah.
dateNote: Reigned two years (2 Kings 15:23), 742–740 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Pekah
summary: Allied with Aram against Judah (the threat behind Isaiah's sign of Immanuel), lost Galilee to Assyria, and was killed by Hoshea.
dateNote: Reigned 20 years (2 Kings 15:27), counted from 752 BC, when he seems to have ruled east of the Jordan as a rival to Menahem; sole king 740–732 BC in Thiele's dating, the years shown.

name: Hoshea
summary: Israel's last king, who rebelled against Assyria; Samaria fell after a three-year siege and Israel was taken into exile.
dateNote: Reigned nine years (2 Kings 17:1), 732–722 BC in Thiele's dating. Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Tiglath-pileser III
summary: Assyrian king who took tribute from Menahem, carried off Galilee's people in Pekah's day, and was paid by Ahaz to rescue Judah from Israel and Aram.
dateNote: King of Assyria 745–727 BC, from his own records. These are his reign.

name: Shalmaneser V
summary: Assyrian king who made Hoshea his vassal, then jailed him for turning to Egypt and besieged Samaria for three years.
dateNote: King of Assyria 727–722 BC. These are his reign; Samaria fell as it ended, and Sargon II claims the conquest.

name: Elijah
summary: Prophet who called down fire on Mount Carmel and was taken to heaven in a whirlwind.

name: Elisha
summary: Elijah's successor, who received a double portion of his spirit and performed many miracles.
dateNote: From Elijah's departure (about 848 BC) to his death under Jehoash of Israel (2 Kings 13:14–20). Years of ministry, approximate.

name: Jonah
summary: Prophet who fled God's call, was swallowed by a great fish, and preached to Nineveh.
dateNote: Prophesied under Jeroboam II (2 Kings 14:25), who reigned 793–753 BC. Scripture doesn't narrow it further.

name: Amos
summary: Shepherd from Tekoa in Judah sent to warn the northern kingdom about injustice and empty worship.
dateNote: In the days of Uzziah and Jeroboam II, two years before the earthquake (Amos 1:1): sometime within 792–753 BC.

name: Hosea
summary: Prophet to the northern kingdom, told to marry Gomer, who was unfaithful to him, as a picture of God's love for faithless Israel.

name: Isaiah
summary: Prophet in Jerusalem through four kings, who foretold judgment, return from exile and the coming servant-king.

name: Micah
summary: Prophet from the Judean countryside who spoke for the poor against Jerusalem's rulers and named Bethlehem as the birthplace of a coming ruler.

name: Hezekiah
summary: Faithful king of Judah who reformed worship and trusted God when Assyria besieged Jerusalem.
dateNote: Twenty-five when he became king, and reigned twenty-nine years (2 Kings 18:2).

name: Sennacherib
summary: Assyrian king who took Judah's fortified cities and besieged Jerusalem in Hezekiah's day, until the angel of the Lord struck his army.
dateNote: King of Assyria 705–681 BC; murdered by his sons, as 2 Kings 19:37 says. These are his reign.

name: Josiah
summary: Boy king who found the Book of the Law in the temple and led Judah's last great reform.
dateNote: Eight when he became king in 640 BC; killed at Megiddo in 609 BC (2 Kings 22:1; 23:29).

name: Pharaoh Neco
summary: Egyptian king who killed Josiah at Megiddo, deposed Jehoahaz and made Jehoiakim king, until Nebuchadnezzar beat him at Carchemish.
dateNote: Neco II, king of Egypt 610–595 BC. These are his reign.

name: Nahum
summary: Prophet from Elkosh who foretold the fall of Nineveh, Assyria's cruel capital.
dateNote: Sometime between the fall of Thebes in 663 BC, which he speaks of as past (Nahum 3:8), and Nineveh's in 612 BC.

name: Zephaniah
summary: Prophet descended from King Hezekiah, who warned of the day of the Lord and promised that God would rejoice over a humble remnant with singing.
dateNote: In the days of Josiah (Zephaniah 1:1), who reigned 640–609 BC.

name: Habakkuk
summary: Prophet who asked God why evil goes unpunished, was told Babylon was coming, and learned that the righteous live by faith.

name: Jeremiah
summary: The "weeping prophet," who warned Jerusalem for forty years before its fall and promised a new covenant.

name: Nebuchadnezzar
summary: King of Babylon (605–562 BC) who destroyed Jerusalem and carried Judah into exile.
dateNote: Reigned 605–562 BC (Babylonian records). Birth year unknown; these are his reign.

name: Zedekiah
summary: Judah's last king, who rebelled against Babylon and was taken there blinded after Jerusalem fell.
dateNote: 21 when he became king; reigned 11 years until Jerusalem fell in 586 BC (2 Kings 24:18).

name: Daniel
summary: Taken to Babylon as a youth, he served its kings and Persia's while staying faithful to God, and saw visions of the kingdoms to come.
dateNote: Taken to Babylon as a youth in 605 BC; still alive in Cyrus's third year, 536 BC (Daniel 10:1).

name: Ezekiel
summary: Priest taken to Babylon in 597 BC, who saw visions of God's glory leaving and returning to the temple.

name: Obadiah
summary: Prophet whose one-chapter book, the shortest in the Old Testament, condemns Edom for turning on Jerusalem in its fall.

name: Belshazzar
summary: Son of Nabonidus and ruler in Babylon, who saw the writing on the wall the night the city fell.
dateNote: Ruled Babylon for his father Nabonidus from about 553 BC until it fell in 539 BC (Nabonidus Chronicle). These are his years of rule.

name: Cyrus the Great
summary: Persian king who conquered Babylon and let the exiles return to rebuild the temple; Isaiah calls him the Lord's anointed.
dateNote: King of Persia 559–530 BC; took Babylon in 539 BC. These are his reign.

name: Zerubbabel
summary: Descendant of David who led the first exiles home and rebuilt the temple.

name: Haggai
summary: Prophet who stirred the returned exiles to finish rebuilding the temple.

name: Zechariah
summary: Prophet who encouraged the temple's rebuilding with visions of God's return to Jerusalem and of a humble king.

name: Darius I
summary: Persian king who confirmed Cyrus's decree and paid for the temple's rebuilding, finished in his sixth year.
dateNote: King of Persia 522–486 BC. These are his reign. Not "Darius the Mede" of Daniel 6, whose identity is debated.

name: Ahasuerus
summary: Persian king (486–465 BC) who made Esther his queen.
dateNote: Reigned 486–465 BC (Ahasuerus in Esther). These are his reign.

name: Esther
summary: Jewish orphan who became queen of Persia and risked her life to save her people.

name: Mordecai
summary: Esther's cousin and guardian, who uncovered Haman's plot and rose to second in the kingdom.

name: Artaxerxes I
summary: Persian king (465–424 BC) who sent Ezra and Nehemiah to Jerusalem.
dateNote: Reigned 465–424 BC. These are his reign.

name: Ezra
summary: Priest and teacher of the Law who led a second group home and called the people back to God's Law.

name: Nehemiah
summary: Cupbearer to Artaxerxes who returned as governor and rebuilt Jerusalem's walls in fifty-two days.

name: Joel
summary: Prophet who saw a plague of locusts as a warning of the day of the Lord, and promised that God would pour out his Spirit on all people.

name: Malachi
summary: The last of the Old Testament prophets, who promised that the Lord would send his messenger before him.

name: Herod the Great
summary: Rome's client king of Judea, a great builder who rebuilt the temple, and the king who tried to kill the infant Jesus.
dateNote: Died in 4 BC, by Josephus's account, at about seventy. King of Judea from 37 BC.

name: Caesar Augustus
summary: First Roman emperor, whose decree for a census brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem.
dateNote: Emperor 27 BC–AD 14, after defeating Antony and Cleopatra in 31 BC. These are his reign.

name: Mary
summary: Young woman of Nazareth who believed the angel's message and bore Jesus; she stood by the cross and prayed with the first believers.

name: Joseph of Nazareth
summary: Descendant of David, betrothed to Mary, who obeyed God's warnings in dreams and raised Jesus in Nazareth.

name: Jesus
summary: The Son of God, born in Bethlehem and raised in Nazareth, who preached the kingdom of God, died on the cross, and rose from the dead.
dateNote: Born before Herod the Great died in 4 BC, probably about 6–4 BC. The crucifixion is dated AD 30 here, when 14 Nisan fell on Friday 7 April; AD 33 (3 April) is the main alternative.

name: John the Baptist
summary: Prophet in the wilderness who called Israel to repent, baptized Jesus, and was beheaded by Herod Antipas.
dateNote: Born about six months before Jesus (Luke 1:36); beheaded by Herod Antipas before the feeding of the five thousand (Mark 6).

name: Peter
summary: Galilean fisherman who became the leader of the twelve apostles; he denied Jesus, was restored, and preached at Pentecost.

name: Mary Magdalene
summary: Follower of Jesus whom he freed from seven demons; she watched the crucifixion and was the first to see him risen.

name: Lazarus
summary: Brother of Mary and Martha in Bethany, whom Jesus raised from the dead after four days in the tomb.

name: Tiberius
summary: Roman emperor through Jesus' ministry; Luke dates John the Baptist's preaching to his fifteenth year.
dateNote: Emperor AD 14–37. These are his reign.

name: Herod Antipas
summary: Herod the Great's son, ruler of Galilee, who beheaded John the Baptist and mocked Jesus before sending him back to Pilate.
dateNote: Tetrarch of Galilee and Perea 4 BC–AD 39, when Caligula exiled him. These are his reign.

name: Pontius Pilate
summary: Roman governor (AD 26–36) who sentenced Jesus to be crucified though he found no guilt in him.
dateNote: Governor of Judea AD 26–36 (Josephus, Tacitus). These are his years in office.

name: Herod Agrippa I
summary: Herod the Great's grandson, who killed James the son of Zebedee and jailed Peter, and died soon after at Caesarea.
dateNote: King of Judea AD 41–44, after ruling lands to the north from AD 37. These are his reign over Judea.

name: Felix
summary: Roman governor who heard Paul's defence at Caesarea and kept him in custody for two years, hoping for a bribe.
dateNote: Governor of Judea about AD 52–59 (Josephus, Tacitus). These are his years in office.

name: Festus
summary: Felix's successor, who heard Paul with King Agrippa II and sent him to Rome when he appealed to Caesar.
dateNote: Governor of Judea about AD 59–62, when he died in office (Josephus). These are his years in office.

name: Nero
summary: The Caesar Paul appealed to, under whom tradition says Paul and Peter were put to death in Rome.
dateNote: Emperor AD 54–68. These are his reign. Scripture doesn't name him; Acts 25:11 calls him Caesar.

name: Stephen
summary: One of the seven chosen to serve the Jerusalem church, and its first martyr.

name: Paul
summary: Pharisee and persecutor of the church who met the risen Jesus, then carried the gospel to the Gentiles across the Roman world and wrote thirteen of the New Testament's letters.
dateNote: Birth estimated: he was a "young man" at Stephen's death (Acts 7:58). Tradition says he was executed in Rome under Nero, about AD 64–67.

name: Cornelius
summary: God-fearing Roman officer at Caesarea, the first Gentile to receive the Spirit through Peter's preaching.

name: Barnabas
summary: "Son of encouragement" from Cyprus, who vouched for Paul and traveled with him on his first journey.

name: James, the Lord's brother
summary: Brother of Jesus who believed after the resurrection, led the church in Jerusalem, and wrote the letter of James.

name: Jude
summary: Brother of James and of Jesus, who believed after the resurrection and wrote the letter of Jude.

name: Silas
summary: Leader of the Jerusalem church who went with Paul on his second journey.

name: Timothy
summary: Young man of Lystra who became Paul's trusted co-worker; two of Paul's letters are written to him.

name: John
summary: Fisherman and one of Jesus' closest disciples; by tradition the author of the Gospel of John, three letters and Revelation.

name: Andrew
summary: Fisherman of Bethsaida, a disciple of John the Baptist, who brought his brother Simon Peter to Jesus.

name: James, son of Zebedee
summary: Fisherman and one of Jesus' three closest disciples; the first apostle to be martyred.

name: Nicodemus
summary: Leader who came to Jesus by night and was told he must be born again; he later helped bury Jesus.

name: Philip the evangelist
summary: One of the seven chosen with Stephen, who preached in Samaria and baptized an Ethiopian official; Paul later stayed at his home in Caesarea.

name: Mark
summary: Cousin of Barnabas who left Paul's first journey but later became his valued helper; by early tradition he wrote down Peter's preaching as the Gospel of Mark.

name: Luke
summary: Doctor and companion of Paul who wrote the Gospel of Luke and the book of Acts.

name: Matthew
summary: Tax collector at Capernaum who left his booth to follow Jesus; by tradition the writer of the first Gospel.

name: Laban
summary: Rebekah's brother in Haran, who gave Jacob his daughters Leah and Rachel and made him work fourteen years for them.

name: Titus
summary: A Greek co-worker of Paul, who carried his letter to Corinth and was left on Crete to appoint elders in every town.
